author: Tarik S. Commons (OpenAI/Codex)
scope: Provisional compatibility of four existing qualified extractions, not new primary extraction or independent approval.

rows.frame_and_window: Retail poultry products; Switzerland/Southern Germany, Aug–Sep2016
rows.ascertainment_and_design: Culture-enriched screen then pure-isolate recovery; product/store probability selection unestablished.
rows.primary_access_basis: Complete publisher PDF previously retrieved; no new primary retrieval in this synthesis.

endpoints.denominator_unit: sample-associated cultures from fresh poultry meat products
endpoints.event: mcr-1 PCR positive in growth on initial selective medium after enrichment
endpoints.not_equivalent_to: 33 confirmed E. coli isolates or direct-PCR positivity of untreated meat

endpoints.event: pure mcr-1 E. coli culture recovered from a sample
discarded during repeated subculture because of mixed Proteus growth
endpoints.classification: unrecovered positive cultures, not negative samples

rows.gene_detection_scope: mcr-1 observed; additional variants absent remains unknown

rows.ascertainment_and_design: All recovered E. coli screened independently of colistin profile; random collection wording does not establish national representativeness.
rows.primary_access_basis: Indexed primary abstract and sections2.1–2.4,3.1–3.3/Table1; full live article not retrieved. Publisher429; direct PMC CAPTCHA.

endpoints.event: mcr gene carriage; 1 mcr-1.1 and 2 mcr-1.2

rows.frame_and_window: Veterinary-hospital convenience recruitment and cohabiting humans; Lisbon, Jan2018–Dec2020
rows.ascertainment_and_design: Selective culture; household clustering and incomplete, participation-dependent longitudinal follow-up.
rows.primary_access_basis: Complete primary JATS previously retrieved; no new primary retrieval in this synthesis.

endpoints.denominator_unit: enrolled companion animals including dogs and cats
endpoints.event: host with recovered mcr-1-positive E. coli during study sampling
host with recovered mcr-1-positive E. coli during study sampling
distinct hosts with recovered mcr-1-positive E. coli during observed follow-up
endpoints.status: arithmetic identification of seed value; not an isolate prevalence or harmonised pooled estimate

endpoints.unit: E. coli isolates/strains from different timepoints

rows.frame_and_window: 40 soil/water/manure samples at eight Oran agricultural sites, May2016–Mar2018
rows.ascertainment_and_design: Enrichment/colistin selection yields a mixed-species bacterial collection; sample/site selection probabilities and positive sample counts unknown.
rows.primary_access_basis: Publisher/indexed primary abstract reached through web search; author-uploaded article text and Table2 exposed in public HTML. Direct publisher open403; PDF not downloaded.

endpoints.interpretation: composition of selected isolate collection, not environmental-sample or farm prevalence

pairwise.reason: Retail product-associated culture/recovery fractions versus gene carriage among recovered E. coli isolates; 570 sampled meats are not the denominator for 3 gene-positive isolates without sample linkage.
Retail product cultures versus human/animal hosts observed during unequal follow-up, with household clustering and repeat-host isolates.
Retail product-associated cultures/recoveries versus a colistin-selected mixed-species bacterial isolate collection; 8/40 sample positivity is not established.
Recovered E. coli isolates screened independently of phenotype versus host carriage under selective culture and unequal longitudinal observation.
All recovered E. coli screened for mcr-1–5 versus selected mixed-species bacterial isolates. Same panel range does not make selection or the reported mcr-1/mcr-3 partition equivalent.
Enrolled hosts clustered in households with repeated sampling versus selected mixed-species isolates clustered within environmental samples/sites.

conclusion: These current fractions do not establish a common cross-sector estimand. Descriptive comparison is possible when units and ascertainment remain explicit; no pooled prevalence or biological sector ranking is estimated.
